versions.name: SQL Server 2025
versions.notes: Current release. First version offering Standard Developer edition alongside Enterprise-based Developer.

versions.name: SQL Server 2022
versions.notes: The most widely deployed current version. Still receiving regular CUs.

versions.name: SQL Server 2019
versions.servicing: Cumulative Updates only (no Service Packs); CU train closed at CU32, security-only updates since
versions.notes: Mainstream support ended 28 February 2025. CU32 was the final cumulative update; patching now means the CU32 + GDR security builds.

versions.name: SQL Server 2017
versions.servicing: First CU-only version (Service Packs ended here); CU train closed at CU31, security-only updates since
versions.notes: In extended support until 12 October 2027. Security fixes still ship as CU31 + GDR builds.

versions.name: SQL Server 2016
versions.servicing: Service Pack model (last version with SPs in practice); CUs shipped per SP, SP3 itself received no CUs

esu.detail: ESU Year 1 runs 2026-07-15 to 2027-07-13; Year 3 ends 2029

versions.notes: Extended support ended 14 July 2026. No more free security updates; Extended Security Updates (paid, or free in Azure) are the only patch path. July 2026 GDRs were the final regular updates.

versions.name: SQL Server 2014
versions.servicing: Service Pack model; CUs shipped per SP
versions.notes: Extended support ended 9 July 2024. Last free security update was the October 2023 GDR. ESU coverage (paid, or free in Azure) runs to mid-2027.

versions.name: SQL Server 2012
versions.servicing: Service Pack model; CUs shipped per SP, SP4 itself received no CUs
versions.notes: Fully out of support, including ESU. The February 2023 SP4 GDR is the last update that will ever ship.
